transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

Any time I have to get blood drawn, I go to great lengths to avoid it or sit there in sheer terror the whole time. It has become a terrible struggle for me, and I was told I should speak to someone about how to handle this fear.
When you face needles or blood draws, do you ever feel faint, actually pass out, or get very dizzy and nauseated?

Yes, I get terribly light-headed and feel like I might pass out, which is terrifying because I actually fainted and broke my wrist during a blood test a year ago. Just seeing a picture of a blood draw makes my heart pound, my hands get clammy, and that awful swooping feeling comes right back. I feel like I'm going to lose consciousness right then and there.
Do you also have this same intense fear or fainting reaction in other situations involving blood, injuries, or medical procedures, or is it mainly with blood draws and needles?

It is really just about having my blood drawn and the needles. Other medical procedures don't bother me, but I actually canceled my cataract surgery solely because they required pre-operative blood tests. The thought of that needle going into my vein is what terrifies me so much.
Do you fear or avoid only blood draws and needles, or do you also have a similar intense fear of seeing blood, injuries, or medical procedures in general?

No, I don't fear seeing blood or injuries in general, nor do other medical procedures bother me. My fear is strictly focused on the needle going into my vein for a blood draw, which started after I fainted and broke my wrist during a test last year. I was actually looking forward to my cataract surgery and only canceled it because of the required pre-operative blood work.
Do you have this same intense fear or fainting reaction with shots, vaccinations, or IVs, or is it only when blood is being drawn from a vein?

It is really just when blood is being drawn from my vein. Regular shots or vaccinations don't trigger this same intense terror for me. My fear is highly focused on the needle going into the vein and the awful worry that I will pass out again, just like when I fell.
Does your fear happen only with blood draws from a vein, or do you also feel the same terror and fainting fear with seeing blood, injuries, or other medical procedures?

It really is just the blood draws from my vein that terrify me, and I don't have this fear with general injuries or other medical procedures. I was actually completely fine with having cataract surgery, and only canceled it because they required those pre-operative labs. It is just that specific needle in my vein that makes me feel like I'm going to pass out.
When you have to get blood drawn, do you avoid it mainly because you fear fainting or losing control, or is it more about being embarrassed, judged, or harmed by the procedure?

Oh, I don't care at all about being embarrassed or judged by anyone. It is entirely because I am terrified of fainting again and breaking another bone, as the needle going into my vein just feels incredibly dangerous and like I am bound to get hurt.
Do you have this fear only when you are facing blood draws, or do you also worry about fainting or feel anxious about it at other times when there is no needle involved?

No, I only worry about fainting or feel this anxiety when it comes to blood draws, or if I see a reminder like a poster of one in a clinic. In my normal daily life, when needles aren't involved, I don't worry about fainting or feel anxious at all.
Do you feel faint or anxious with other needle-related procedures too, such as injections, vaccinations, or IV placement, or is it only when blood is being drawn from a vein?

I'm not really sure about other needle procedures like injections or vaccinations, as I haven't really thought about them. My terror is completely tied to that one awful time I fainted and broke my wrist during a blood draw from my vein, which is the only thing I dread.
When you think about needles, is it only blood draws from a vein that scare you, or do injections, vaccinations, and IV placement also trigger the same fear or fainting feeling?

Yes, it is strictly the blood draws from my vein that trigger this terror. Regular injections or vaccinations don't seem to cause this fear for me at all. My anxiety is entirely focused on the needle going into the vein because of that awful time I fainted.
Do you ever have this same intense fear or fainting reaction in other situations where you are not getting blood drawn, or is it only when you face a blood draw from a vein?

No, it is strictly limited to blood draws, seeing pictures of them, or knowing a needle is about to go into my vein. I never experience this intense fear or light-headedness in any other unrelated situations. Outside of those specific moments, I feel completely fine.
Do you also get the same fear or fainting feeling with seeing blood, injuries, or other medical procedures, or is it only when a needle goes into your vein for a blood draw?

It is strictly when a needle goes into my vein for a blood draw, not with general injuries or other procedures. Even seeing a picture of a blood draw can trigger that awful light-headedness, but it is specifically the needle in the vein that terrifies me because of my past fall. Other medical situations do not bother me at all.
Do you also feel this same fear or fainting reaction with injections, vaccinations, or IV placement, or is it only when blood is drawn from a vein?

I'm not entirely sure about injections, vaccinations, or IVs since I haven't had any of those recently. But I know for certain that my intense fear and fainting reaction are definitely triggered by having blood drawn from my vein.
Do you ever get the same intense fear or fainting feeling with injections, vaccinations, or IV placement, or is it only when blood is drawn from a vein?

As I mentioned, I am really not sure about vaccinations or other injections since I haven't had them recently. I just know for certain that my fear is definitely triggered by blood draws and having a needle go into my vein.
Do you ever feel faint or panicky when you see blood, injuries, or get other shots, or is it only with blood being drawn from a vein?

It is strictly with blood being drawn from my vein, or seeing pictures of it, rather than general injuries or other shots. This is because it immediately reminds me of that awful time I fainted and broke my wrist. Other than that specific situation, I don't get that faint or panicky feeling at all.
When you think about the blood draw, is the main fear the pain of the needle, the sight of blood, or the chance that you will faint and get injured again?

The main fear is definitely fainting and getting injured again. A year ago, I fainted during a routine blood test, fell, and broke my wrist, which was just terrible for my independence. Now, just the thought of the needle makes me feel light-headed and terrified that I will pass out and hurt myself all over again.
Does your fear happen only when you are having blood drawn from a vein, or does it also happen with injections, vaccinations, IVs, or even just seeing blood or injuries?

It is strictly tied to having blood drawn from my vein, or seeing pictures of it, because of that awful time I fainted and broke my wrist. I don't experience this fear with regular injections, vaccinations, or seeing blood and injuries in general. It is just that specific needle in my vein that terrifies me so much.
When you think about needles, is the fear mainly about blood draws from a vein specifically, or do injections, vaccinations, and IV placement also cause the same intense fear or fainting feeling?

It is highly specific to blood draws and having a needle go into my vein, which all traces back to when I fainted and broke my wrist. Regular injections or vaccinations don't trigger this same level of intense terror or fainting feeling for me. My mind is just completely fixated on the danger of having blood drawn from my vein.

Have you ever had a similar fear or fainting reaction with other things that involve seeing blood or injuries, like watching someone get hurt or seeing an open wound, or is it only with blood draws from a vein?

No, I don't have any reaction to seeing open wounds or other people getting hurt; it is strictly tied to blood draws from my vein. It all started when I fainted and broke my wrist during that test, and now even seeing a picture of a blood draw triggers that light-headedness. General injuries or seeing blood from a cut don't bother me at all.

When you are in the blood-draw situation, is your main fear actually the needle or pain, or is it specifically the feeling of fainting and losing control? Also, do you tend to feel better if you lie down during it?

My fear is tied to both, because the needle going into my vein feels incredibly dangerous, and I am absolutely terrified of feeling that swooping light-headedness and passing out again like when I fell. As for lying down, I usually just sit in the chair gripping the armrests with my eyes squeezed shut, so I haven't actually tried that and don't know if it would help.
When you need a blood draw, do you ever actually faint or nearly faint, and does lying down during the procedure reduce the light-headedness or fear?

Yes, I did actually faint that one time a year ago when I fell and broke my wrist, and now I constantly feel like I am right on the verge of passing out again. I have never actually tried lying down during the procedure, though, so I'm not sure if it would help with the fear or the light-headedness.
When you are getting a blood draw, do you ever have warning signs like nausea, sweating, or tunnel vision right before fainting, or does the fear mainly stay as panic without those physical symptoms?

Yes, I definitely experience physical symptoms rather than just panic. My heart starts pounding, my hands get very clammy, and I start shaking while sitting in the chair. I also get that same swooping light-headedness that makes me feel like I am about to pass out right then and there.
Do you have this same fear or fainting reaction with other things that involve blood, injuries, or medical procedures, or is it only when you are having blood drawn from a vein?

It is strictly tied to having blood drawn from my vein, or seeing pictures of it, which all stems from when I fainted and broke my wrist. Other medical procedures don't bother me at all; for instance, I was perfectly fine with having cataract surgery and only canceled it because of the required pre-operative blood work.
Does the fear happen with other needle procedures too, like injections, vaccinations, or IV placement, or is it only when blood is drawn from a vein?

It is strictly the blood draw itself and the needle going into my vein that triggers this intense terror, which all goes back to when I fainted and broke my wrist. Ordinary shots or vaccinations don't cause this reaction for me at all. It is really just the vein aspect of the blood draw that feels so dangerous.
Does your fear also happen with other needle procedures like IV placement or injections, or is it only when blood is drawn from a vein?

I'm not quite sure about other needle procedures like IVs or injections because I haven't really had to think about them. All of my focus and dread have been entirely on the blood draws and having needles put in my veins for my lab work.
